title: Fan-to-Duct Connection Chooser
description: Scenario recommender: for eight illustrative job descriptions in a fixed order, the learner selects one of seven connection and inlet box options (bolted flange, slip connection, flexible connector, tube adapter and rubber sleeve, bolt-on inlet box, free-standing inlet box, inlet box horn) and submits it once; definitions can be opened at any time, feedback gives the deciding fact, and a summary lists every answer beside the accepted answers.

educational.audience: Adult professional development: new application engineers, sales staff, representatives and facilities staff
educational.topic: Connecting a fan to its ductwork
learningObjectives: The learner will use the support, alignment, temperature and pressure facts in a job description to choose the inlet box style or fan-to-duct connection that fits it, with at least 7 of 8 correct on the first attempt.

accessibility.notes: describe() text (fallback mode); job text, selections, definitions, verdicts and the summary are announced through FP.announce (aria-live); options are native aria-pressed toggle buttons; ✓/✗ glyphs and solid/dashed borders pair with colour; keys 1-7 select an option, D opens its definition, Enter submits and then goes to the next job.

controls.label: 1-7 options
controls.purpose: Select a connection or inlet box option for the current job (keys 1-7)

controls.label: Definition
controls.purpose: Open or hide the definition of the selected option (D); exploration, not scored

controls.label: Submit
controls.purpose: Lock in the selected option; the first submission is scored (Enter)

controls.label: Next
controls.purpose: Go to the next job; after job 8, See summary (Enter)

controls.label: Start over
controls.purpose: Clear all answers and the score

rules: Tube adapter sleeve acceptable when pressure <= 5 psi and temperature <= 180°F; otherwise not acceptable
An answer is correct when it is any entry in the job's Accepted answers (job 2 accepts slip connection or flexible connector)
Each job is scored on its first submission only; mastery is 7 of 8
Jobs appear in the fixed order of the chapter's Content table, so jobs 3 and 4 are back to back
assumptions: Job 4's pipe flange is a 125# ASA flange of the same nominal size as the blower outlet
limitations: Job descriptions are illustrative scenarios, not specific orders

sources: FanPedia: The Fan & Blower Encyclopedia, pp. 67, 126, 127, 131, 132, 141, 142, 143, 187, 194
Chapter 19 section "Connecting the Fan to the Duct"

pedagogical.teachingStrategy: Find the deciding fact (isolation, separate support, a temperature limit, intersecting airflows) in a job description and act on it
keyQuestions: Which fact in the job description decides the connection?
commonMisconceptions: A rubber sleeve connector can be used at any temperature.
A bolted joint is fine on a spring-isolated fan.
Any detached inlet box is supported by the fan.
A horn is a sound-control device.
assessmentOpportunities: Running count 'Correct: n of 8'; mastery is 7 of 8 correct on the first attempt; the summary reads 'Mastery: 7 or more of 8' or 'Review the sections on the items you missed.' Opening definitions is exploration, not evidence.
